# Mikhail Basov

> Mikhail Basov (Михаил Басов, also written Michael Basov) is a Senior DevOps Engineer at Sberbank. He administers 24 Kubernetes clusters, builds release automation, and fixes alerting rules in open-source monitoring projects such as Grafana Mimir, Ceph and Rook.

Canonical profile: https://mikhailbasov.github.io/
Russian version: https://mikhailbasov.github.io/ru/
Updated: 2026-11-10

## Facts

- Role: Senior DevOps Engineer at Sberbank, Risk Division. DevOps Engineer there since February 2024, Senior since July 2026.
- Scope: administers 24 Kubernetes clusters, from dev to production, and runs 70+ microservices in production under a 99.9% SLO.
- Experience: 5+ years in production infrastructure. Before Sberbank: Systems Engineer at USSC (Ural Security Systems Center), January 2022 to February 2024, deploying DLP and PAM systems; System Administrator at IT-Service, May 2021 to January 2022.
- Education: Ural Federal University, BSc in Software Engineering, part-time, expected in 2027. Polzunov College, Diploma in Information Security, 2022.
- Languages: English and Russian.
- Award: Engineering Achievement of the Year 2025, Sberbank (internal), for the AI code reviewer. Letter of appreciation: https://mikhail-basov-docs.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/index.html?lang=en
- Stack: Jenkins (Groovy shared libraries), Argo CD (GitOps), Helm, Nexus, Jira, Git, SAST/SCA; Kubernetes, OpenShift, Docker, Istio; Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, Dynatrace; Python, Groovy, Bash, Linux, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka; AWS, Terraform, Ansible; AI code review and LLM agents in production, MCP, RAG (pgvector).

## In numbers

- 24: Kubernetes clusters he administers, from dev to production.
- About 150: releases a week that go to production through his rollout service.
- 1,200+: pull requests a day at peak for the AI code reviewer he built.
- 17: merged pull requests in 10 open-source projects.

## Work at Sberbank

- Release platform: built and owns the release platform of the Risk division. It assembles a release from Jira tasks, attaches the builds from Nexus and takes the release through quality gates. Coordinating a release took 2-4 hours and now takes under 10 minutes. About 40 teams use it.
- Unattended rollout: his rollout service deploys about 150 releases a week to production, at night and on weekends. 86% of production installs start without a person. Rollout goes in waves: each wave re-checks the approval, and a failed wave stops the ones after it.
- Kubernetes and CI/CD: moved the team's services and their CI from OpenShift to Kubernetes; writes their Helm charts, which Argo CD deploys, and Jenkins pipelines on Groovy shared libraries with SAST and SCA scans; resolves incidents and writes RCAs.
- AI code reviewer: proposed and shipped an AI reviewer for pull requests in Bitbucket. At peak it reviews 1,200+ pull requests a day with a median response of about 30 seconds. It started as a Jenkins job and became a Python service on Kubernetes.

## Research

- "Silent or Wrong: Producer-Contract Defects in Shipped Prometheus Alerting Rules". Alerting rules shipped with exporters, Helm charts and monitoring mixins often depend on facts about their metrics (units, types, labels, histogram buckets) that the rule never states; when such a fact is wrong, the alert never fires or fires on the wrong condition. He audited 1,808 shipped rules from 86 rule sets and confirmed 31 distinct defects. In at least 19 of them the alert cannot fire in the situation it was written for; promtool and Pint in offline mode find none of the 31. Mikhail Basov chose the topic, designed the study and ran it with LLM agents under his supervision. Submitted to arXiv (cs.SE) in November 2026.

## Bio

Mikhail Basov is a Senior DevOps Engineer at Sberbank, where he administers 24 Kubernetes clusters and runs 70+ microservices in production. He built the release platform and the rollout service behind about 150 production releases a week, and an AI code reviewer that handles 1,200+ pull requests a day at peak. He has 17 merged pull requests in open-source projects such as Grafana Mimir, Ceph and Rook, and wrote a study of defects in shipped Prometheus alerting rules.
